title: USB device: CDC, HID, MSC, and custom classes

spans.text: A USB device is the peripheral connected to a computer. Boards with USB peripheral hardware, such as ESP32-S2/S3, can expose serial, keyboard, storage, or a custom interface.

CDC provides serial diagnostics and simple host communication; HID implements standard keyboard/mouse interfaces; MSC can expose the device's flash storage as a disk. A composite device presents several interfaces over one cable. A custom/vendor interface needs matching host-side software or a driver.

The Arduino-ESP32 USB API requires a chip with USB peripheral hardware. Start with the core's native CDC example; use its HID, MSC, and composite examples and confirm the USB Mode setting. Descriptor fields such as
do not change the physical power output.

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: Requires a compatible board with USB peripheral hardware; check Tools/USB Mode and pin wiring. HID creates real input: send a harmless character from an explicit physical action, never hidden keystroke sequences. Power loss during MSC writes can corrupt a filesystem.
